analysis.title: I wanna be in the room where it happens
key_insights: The Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral talks at APEC ended with a joint declaration with four points: UN reform, higher refined petroleum production and supply, state consent and immunity for officials against the ICC, and that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. Rabobank says the commitments mean nothing at face value.

The meeting has raised concern that a partial 'Yalta' could reshape geopolitics, geoeconomics and markets, with the US, Russia and China leading the world order and Europe, or at least Ukraine, sidelined.
The FT reports Putin opened the door to inviting European leaders to Moscow to discuss the war in Ukraine. Putin did not commit to a formal role for them in a peace process.
German Chancellor Merz called the Yalta format unable to bring peace to Ukraine and described the summit as a photo op.
The USD kept dominating FX markets. DXY climbed to levels not seen since 2025 on elevated US hiking expectations and safe-haven demand.
The S&P 500 fell more than 147 points (2.02%) and the Nasdaq fell 2.2%, despite the Anthropic IPO closing 17.1% above its IPO price. US Treasury yields fell across the curve in the risk-off move.
Emerging market currencies fell more than other currencies because safe-haven USD demand combined with falling carry attractiveness.

The OIS curve prices a full hike in December and close to 70% of a 25bp hike in January. Waller's recent calls are for a 50bp hike in December, or a 25bp hike with clear forward guidance from Warsh that another hike follows in January.
Waller's call conflicts with Warsh's philosophy of avoiding forward guidance. The FOMC meets December 9.

Day ahead: final November UMich data are due, with current conditions expected to rise from 51.0 to 52.3. Trump holds a press conference at noon ET on the APEC takeaways. Canadian and Mexican retail sales are also due.
